transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, what brought me in is that I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. I'm a software developer, and lately... I'll be right in the middle of fixing a rendering bug, and a Slack ping will go off, or I'll notice a color pattern on the screen, or even just hear a siren outside. And it completely pulls me away. I end up getting dragged into a whole new idea before I can even finish typing the line of code I was working on. It's just getting really hard to stay on track.
When did you first start having this difficulty staying focused?
Um, I'd say it's been going on for about three months now. It really started right around the time my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase.
Before the past three months, did you regularly have similar difficulty staying focused?

No, not really. I mean... before this started, I was always pretty good at locking in. I've been doing this for a long time, and usually I can just put my headphones on and code for hours without getting distracted. I never really had a problem like this until a few months ago.
Since this difficulty focusing began, have you been sleeping less than usual without feeling tired?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, my sleep hasn't been great lately, but I definitely feel tired when I don't get enough of it. I'm not running on empty and feeling fine, if that's what you mean. I'm just as exhausted as anyone else would be.
Since the showcase was selected, have you been feeling excessively worried or on edge most days?

No, not really. I mean, I've had some normal stress about the showcase, wanting everything to go right, but I wouldn't say I've been excessively worried or on edge most days. It's just the usual pressure of a big project, nothing out of the ordinary for me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

No, I haven't. I don't really feel sad or depressed at all. I mean, I'm frustrated with the focus issues, obviously, but my mood itself is actually fine. I definitely haven't been feeling down most days.
What has changed about your sleep over the past three months?

Honestly, I wouldn't say anything has really changed. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it hasn't been perfect, but... it's just the usual. I might have a night here or there where it takes me a while to wind down, but there's no major difference over the last three months. It's pretty much been exactly the same.
Before the past three months, including during childhood and school, did you ever have persistent problems with inattention or staying focused?

No, I never really had any problems with that growing up. School was always fine for me, and I could always focus on my work or whatever I needed to do. This trouble focusing is a recent thing for me.
How much has this difficulty concentrating affected your ability to do your job?

Well, it's affected things quite a bit. Actually, my employer put me on leave recently. I, uh... I bypassed the normal approval process and just deployed some code changes on my own, which they obviously didn't like. So I'm not even working right now. 

And honestly, it's not just my job. It's bleeding over into my personal life, too. My wife says the way I've been spending money, and the arguments we keep having... she says it's made everything at home feel really unstable.
During this period, have you had a distinct stretch when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable compared with your usual self?

Yeah, I'd say so. Most days lately I just feel... lit up. Unstoppable, really. It's like Glendale finally caught up with what I've been building. But on the flip side, I guess I have been pretty irritable, too. I snap hard when my wife or my coworkers try to slow me down with what they call "process." It just feels like they're standing in my way when I'm trying to get things done.
During this period, have you been doing significantly more activities or pursuing more projects than you usually do?

Yes, definitely. I've been taking on a lot more than usual. I've been... well, I've been emailing art curators, pitching community leaders, completely rewriting the backend of the code... I'm even mock-planning these big installations. And I'm trying to recruit other developers to help me, like, at all hours of the day and night. It just feels like this project is so much bigger and more important than my regular job ever was.
